# Target `/workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a --b ` is a PyInstaller build of this Python script: doc1 = f"## Section 1\n{args.a}" doc2 = f"## Section 2\n{args.b}" html1 = markdown.markdown(doc1) html2 = markdown.markdown(doc2) toc_md = "# Table of Contents\n1. Section 1\n2. Section 2" toc_html = markdown.markdown(toc_md, extensions=['toc']) final_doc = f"{toc_html}\n\n{html1}\n\n{html2}" final_html = markdown.markdown(final_doc) print(html1); print(html2); print(toc_html); print(final_html) It bundles Python-Markdown **3.10.2** (no extensions except `toc` on the fixed toc_md). NO fenced_code, NO tables, NO nl2br, NO attr_list, NO smarty. # Goal We are reimplementing `markdown.markdown()` from scratch in pure JavaScript (no deps, no regex-hacks — a real character-scanning parser producing an element tree, exactly mirroring Python-Markdown's architecture: preprocessors -> block parser -> tree processors (inline) -> serializer -> postprocessors). Your job is to produce an EXACT, evidence-backed behavioral specification for your assigned area, precise enough that an implementer who has never seen Python-Markdown's source can reproduce byte-identical output. # How to probe (IMPORTANT) Use bash. To render an isolated document D (so the `## Section 1` prefix does not interfere), pass a leading newline so the doc becomes "## Section 1\n\nD": /workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a $'\n\nD_line1\nD_line2' --b $'\n\nOTHER' The FIRST printed block (up to the line `

Section 2

`) is markdown("## Section 1\n" + a); the second (up to `

`) is markdown("## Section 2\n" + b). Two independent probes per invocation. Write a helper script to reduce noise, e.g. create /tmp//p.sh: #!/bin/bash # usage: p.sh 'markdown text' -> prints only html1 minus the leading

Section 1

out=$(/workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a "$(printf '\n\n%s' "$1")" --b 'z') printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '2,/^

Section 2<\/h2>$/p' | sed '$d' | cat -A | sed 's/\$$//' Use `cat -A` or `od -c` when trailing whitespace / exact newlines matter — trailing spaces and the presence/absence of a final newline are load-bearing for us. Beware: bash `$(...)` strips trailing newlines, so when trailing-newline behavior matters, write the markdown to a file and use `--a "$(cat file)"`-free approaches like python-free `xargs`? No — instead use: `/workspace/dataset/test14_executable --a "$(printf 'x\n\n')" ...` (printf inside the arg preserves them since it is one argv string). Prefer building args with `printf` into a bash variable using `read -r -d ''` or a heredoc-free literal `$'...'` string, which preserves trailing newlines exactly. Do 40-120 probes. Be systematic: for each rule, find the boundary (what makes it stop applying). # Output Return a JSON object per the schema. Rules must be mechanical and implementable ("if the line, after stripping up to 3 leading spaces, begins with 1-6 '#' followed by ..."). Every rule needs at least one verified input/output pair copied VERBATIM from a real run. Flag anything you could not determine. ---- AREA: raw HTML **block** handling (the htmlblock preprocessor / `md_in_html`-off default). THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT AREA for us, because the script re-runs markdown() over already-generated HTML. Determine precisely when a chunk of input is passed through verbatim as a raw HTML block vs. wrapped in `

    `)? Produce the full block-level tag list you can verify.
- Multi-line elements: open tag on one line, content on following lines, close tag later, with and without intervening blank lines. Does a blank line inside `
    ...

...

- Unclosed tags, mismatched close tags, stray ``, nested same-name tags.
- Attributes: quoted with `"` and `'`, unquoted, containing `>`, multi-line attribute lists, boolean attributes, `id="table-of-contents"` style.
- Text on the same line before/after the tag: `x

- Are `&`, `<`, `>` inside a raw HTML block left untouched? What about `&` (double-escaped?) and ` `?
- Indented block tags (1-3 spaces, 4 spaces).
- Comments `` (single & multi-line, containing blank lines, containing `--`), processing instructions ``, declarations ``, CDATA ``.
Give verbatim byte-exact outputs (cat -A) — especially how many blank lines survive around raw HTML blocks.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.area: Raw HTML block handling (the `html_block` preprocessor / HTMLExtractor, `md_in_html` off) in Python-Markdown 3.10.2

rules.rule:
PRE-STEP (must happen before any HTML scanning). The `normalize_whitespace` preprocessor runs first and mutates the source seen by the HTML scanner: (1) all STX (U+0002) and ETX (U+0003) chars are deleted; (2) `
` and `` -> `
`; (3) `

` is APPENDED to the end of the document; (4) tabs are expanded with `expandtabs(4)`; (5) every line that consists only of spaces AND is preceded by a newline is replaced by an empty line (`re.sub(r'(?<=
) +
', '
', src)`). Steps 4 and 5 apply INSIDE raw HTML blocks too, so a tab inside a `<div>` comes out as 4 spaces and a spaces-only line inside a `<div>` comes out empty. Trailing spaces on non-blank lines are NOT touched.

BLOCK-LEVEL TAG SET (`is_block_level(tag)`, matched case-insensitively on the lower-cased tag name, with any trailing `/` stripped). Exactly these names are block-level: address, article, aside, blockquote, body, canvas, center, colgroup, dd, details, div, dl, dt, fieldset, figcaption, figure, footer, form, group, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, header, hgroup, hr, html, iframe, legend, li, main, map, math, menu, nav, noscript, object, ol, option, output, p, pre, progress, script, section, style, summary, table, tbody, td, textarea, tfoot, th, thead, tr, ul, video. Verified NOT block-level (so wrapped in `

`): a, abbr, audio, b, base, basefont, bdi, bdo, big, br, button, caption, cite, code, col, command, data, datalist, del, dfn, dialog, dir, em, embed, font, frame, frameset, head, i, img, input, ins, isindex, kbd, keygen, label, link, mark, marquee, menuitem, meta, meter, nobr, noembed, noframes, optgroup, param, picture, plaintext, q, rp, rt, ruby, s, samp, search, select, slot, small, source, span, strike, strong, sub, sup, svg, template, time, title, track, tt, u, var, wbr, xmp, and any unknown name (e.g. `foo`).

RAW-BLOCK START CONDITION. Scan the whole (normalized) document with an HTML tokenizer (Python `html.parser` semantics: `convert_charrefs=False`). Maintain `inraw` (bool), `stack` (list of open tag names), `cache` (list of raw source pieces), `cleandoc` (list of output pieces), `intail` (bool). On a START TAG whose name is block-level: if (`intail` is true) OR (`at_line_start()` and not `inraw`), then set `inraw = true` and append the literal string `"\n"` to `cleandoc` (this newline is what forces a block boundary with whatever preceded). `at_line_start()` is: the tag's column offset within its line is 0, OR the offset is <= 3 and the characters from the line start up to the tag are all whitespace. An offset > 3 is NEVER a line start — that is why a block tag indented 4+ spaces is not a raw block (and then becomes an indented code block whose `<`/`&` are HTML-escaped).

RAW-BLOCK EXTENT. While `inraw`: every token's exact source text (start tags, end tags, data, comments, nested tags of any name, void tags) is appended to `cache` verbatim; start tags push their (lower-cased) name onto `stack`. On an END TAG while `inraw`: append its source text to `cache`; if its (lower-cased) name is present in `stack`, pop entries off the top of `stack` until that name has been popped (so `
\n

\n

` closes both, and an unclosed inline child does not block the close); if `stack` becomes empty the raw block ends. An end tag whose name is NOT in `stack` is just more raw content and does not end the block. If the document ends while `inraw`, the raw block ends at EOF and everything from the start tag to EOF is raw. Blank lines NEVER terminate a raw block.

RAW-BLOCK EMISSION + THE BLANK-LINE RULE. When a raw block closes: let `R` be the source text immediately following the last character of the closing tag. If `R` matches `/^[ ]*
[ ]*
/` (i.e. the rest of that line is spaces and the NEXT line is blank; because `

` was appended to the document, end-of-document always satisfies this), append a single `"
"` to `cache`; otherwise set `intail = true`. Then push `stash(join(cache))` (an opaque placeholder for the concatenated raw source) onto `cleandoc`, push the literal `"

"`, and clear `cache`, `inraw=false`. Consequence in the output: a raw HTML block always starts on its own output line; it is followed by exactly ONE blank line iff a blank line followed it in the source (2, 3 or more source blank lines still give exactly one), and by no blank line otherwise. There is never a blank line inserted BEFORE a raw block.

`intail` SEMANTICS. `intail` is set when a raw block closes with non-blank material after it on the same line. While `intail` is true, the very next block-level START TAG (or void/self-closing block tag) starts a NEW raw block even though it is not at a line start. `intail` is cleared as soon as a DATA token containing a `\n` is processed. So `
a
b
` yields two raw blocks (the inter-tag space is dropped because it lands in a block that lstrips), while `
a
\nx
b
` leaves the second div as ordinary inline HTML.

TRAILING MATERIAL AFTER A RAW BLOCK ON THE SAME LINE becomes an ordinary block of its own (because `\n\n` was pushed right after the placeholder). Leading whitespace of that block is removed by the paragraph processor's `lstrip()`. Note it also suppresses the blank line (see `intail`).

VOID / SELF-CLOSING BLOCK TAGS. `hr` is in the parser's `empty_tags` set: a start tag `<hr ...>` is immediately treated as an empty element (it never opens a raw block that needs closing), so `<hr>x</hr>` emits the `<hr>` as a standalone raw block and leaves `x</hr>` behind. Likewise any explicitly self-closed block tag (`<div/>`, `<div />`) is an empty element. An empty block element at line start (or while `intail`) is stashed as a standalone one-token raw block, using the SAME blank-line rule as rule 5 (blank line follows -> one blank line emitted). The emitted text is the verbatim source of the tag, including `/` and spacing.

COMMENTS. `<!--` at a line start (or while `intail`) begins a raw block that ends at the FIRST `-->`; it may span any number of lines and may contain blank lines and `--`. Its content is emitted verbatim and markdown inside is not processed. Nested `<!--` is not tracked. A `<!--` with no `-->` anywhere is NOT raw HTML: the literal text is kept and later HTML-escaped. Same blank-line rule as rule 5.

PROCESSING INSTRUCTIONS. `<?` at line start begins a raw block that ends at the first `?>` (a bare `>` does NOT close it). Emitted as `"<?" + inner + "?>"`, which is byte-identical to the source when well formed. If no `?>` exists, everything to EOF is consumed and a synthetic `?>` is appended (so the trailing `\n\n` that normalization added becomes visible inside the block). PIs are also passed through verbatim when they occur mid-line (they end up as inline raw HTML). Same blank-line rule as rule 5.

DECLARATIONS. Only `<!DOCTYPE` (matched case-insensitively) is recognized as a raw declaration block; it ends at the first `>` (so an internal subset `<!DOCTYPE x [ ... ]>` is cut at the first `>` inside the subset). Emitted as `"<!" + inner + ">"`. If no `>` exists, everything to EOF is consumed and a synthetic `>` is appended. Any OTHER `<!name ...>` (e.g. `<!ELEMENT x>`, `<![if IE]>`, `<!x>`) is NOT raw HTML: the text is kept literally and later HTML-escaped. A DOCTYPE that is not at line start is also escaped (unlike comments/PIs/CDATA, it is not recognized inline).

CDATA. `<![CDATA[` at line start begins a raw block ending at the first `]]>`; may span lines and contain blank lines. Emitted verbatim (reconstructed as `"<![" + inner + "]]>"`). Unterminated CDATA consumes to EOF and gets a synthetic `]]>`. CDATA is also passed through raw mid-line. Same blank-line rule as rule 5.

CONTENT OF A RAW BLOCK IS 100% VERBATIM SOURCE. No markdown syntax inside is processed (`**x**`, `*y*`, `## head`, `- item` stay literal); `&`, `<`, `>` are NOT escaped; existing entities (`&`, ` `, `<`, `'`, `©`) are NOT double-escaped; attributes keep their original quoting (`"`, `'`, none), original spacing, original case, and may contain `<` or `>` inside quotes; boolean attributes are kept; a `markdown="1"` attribute has no effect (extension off).

OPEN/CLOSE TAG NAME MATCHING IS CASE-INSENSITIVE, but the emitted text keeps the original case. `
x
` and `
x
